/-!
# Erdős Problem 189

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/189](https://www.erdosproblems.com/189)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Affine EuclideanGeometry

namespace Erdos189

/-- Erdős problem 189 asked whether the below holds for all rectangles. -/
def Erdos189For (P : ℝ² → ℝ² → ℝ² → ℝ² → Prop) (A : ℝ² → ℝ² → ℝ² → ℝ² → ℝ) :=
    ∀ᵉ (n > 0) (colouring : ℝ² → Fin n), ∃ colour, ∀ area > (0 : ℝ), ∃ a b c d,
      {a, b, c, d} ⊆ colouring⁻¹' {colour} ∧
      IsCcwConvexPolygon ![a, b, c, d] ∧
      A a b c d = area ∧
      P a b c d

/--
If $\mathbb{R}^2$ is finitely coloured then must there exist some colour class which contains the
vertices of a rectangle of every area?

Graham, "On Partitions of 𝔼ⁿ", Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series A 28, 89-91 (1980).
(See "Concluding Remarks" on page 96.)

Solved (with answer `False`, as formalised below) in:
Vjekoslav Kovač, "Coloring and density theorems for configurations of a given volume", 2023
https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.09973
In fact, Kovač's colouring is even Jordan measurable (the topological boundary of each
monochromatic region is Lebesgue measurable and has measure zero).

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev and Kovac using Aristotle.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 51, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.24.0/ErdosProblems/Erdos189.lean"]
theorem erdos_189 :
    answer(False) ↔ Erdos189For
      (fun a b c d ↦
        line[ℝ, a, b].direction ⟂ line[ℝ, b, c].direction ∧
        line[ℝ, b, c].direction ⟂ line[ℝ, c, d].direction ∧
        line[ℝ, c, d].direction ⟂ line[ℝ, d, a].direction)
      (fun a b c d ↦ dist a b * dist b c) := by
  sorry

/-- Graham claims this is "easy to see". -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 51]
theorem erdos_189.variants.square :
    ¬ Erdos189For
      (fun a b c d ↦
        line[ℝ, a, b].direction ⟂ line[ℝ, b, c].direction ∧
        line[ℝ, b, c].direction ⟂ line[ℝ, c, d].direction ∧
        line[ℝ, c, d].direction ⟂ line[ℝ, d, a].direction ∧
        dist a b = dist b c)
      (fun a b c d ↦ dist a b * dist b c) := by
  sorry

/--
Seems to be open, as of January 2025.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 51]
theorem erdos_189.variants.parallelogram :
    ¬ Erdos189For
      (fun a b c d ↦
        line[ℝ, a, b] ∥ line[ℝ, c, d] ∧
        line[ℝ, a, d] ∥ line[ℝ, b, c])
      (fun a b c d ↦ dist a b * dist b c * (∡ a b c).sin) := by
  sorry

end Erdos189

findings.description: The declaration directly asserts `¬ Erdos189For ...`, thereby fixing a negative answer: some finite colouring has no colour class containing parallelograms of every positive area. The cited sources pose an undecided yes-or-no question, not this negative conjecture. There is no `answer(sorry)` slot here, so this is not merely an equivalent negated question with an inverted unknown answer. The existing `research open` tag is consistent with the source; the issue is the statement's commitment to one answer.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős–Graham, Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number Theory (1980), p. 15: “The question is: Is this also true for rectangles? or perhaps parallelograms?” (https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/80_11_number_theory.pdf). Kovač, arXiv:2309.09973v3, §1.3, explicitly asks whether a colour class must contain parallelograms of every given area and says the question remains unanswered. https://www.erdosproblems.com/189 likewise states: “The question for parallelograms remains open.”
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the leading `¬` with `answer(sorry) ↔`, retaining the geometric predicate, area expression, and `research open` tag. Alternatively, `answer(sorry) ↔ ¬ Erdos189For ...` would faithfully pose the negated question without fixing its answer.

findings.description: The docstring's Graham reference gives the page range as 89–91. The paper occupies pages 89–97; the separately cited Concluding Remarks on page 96 are correctly located. This is only a bibliographic slip.
findings.source_evidence: Graham's publication list, 1980 item 3, records “On Partitions of E^n,” Journal of Combinatorial Theory (A) 28 (1980), 89–97 (https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/). Kovač's bibliography entry `Gra80` also gives 89–97, and the nine-page original scan ends on page 97: https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/80_03_partitions.pdf.

reformulations.difference: The area representation uses the oriented-angle sine `(∡ a b c).sin` without an absolute value, rather than the usual sine of the unoriented interior angle. This entry concerns only the geometry, independently of the answer-choice defect above.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: `IsCcwConvexPolygon ![a,b,c,d]` requires `(∡ a b c).sign = 1`. Thus its sine is strictly positive, and Mathlib's `oangle_eq_angle_of_sign_eq_one` identifies this oriented angle with the unoriented angle. Consequently the supplied area equals both `dist a b * dist b c * Real.sin (∠ a b c)` and the absolute-sine version. In scratch.lean I proved the full `Erdos189For P signedArea ↔ Erdos189For P ordinaryArea` equivalence for arbitrary P, as well as the absolute-sine equivalent. Negating the predicates preserves these equivalences.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/189 — statement, variants and current status, read through https://r.jina.ai/https://www.erdosproblems.com/189
https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.09973 — abstract, version history and publication metadata
https://arxiv.org/e-print/2309.09973 — v3 LaTeX source, especially §§1.2–1.3, §2 and the bibliography
R. L. Graham, On Partitions of E^n, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 28 (1980), 89–97, especially p. 96: https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/80_03_partitions.pdf
P. Erdős and R. L. Graham, Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number Theory (1980), p. 15: https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/80_11_number_theory.pdf
https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/ — publication list, 1980 item 3, read through its r.jina.ai rendering
review.notes: Checked all four declarations and their supporting geometric definitions. The rectangle statement and square variant have the intended geometry and quantifiers. Scratch proofs verify pairwise distinctness, positive area, exclusion of collapsed quadrilaterals, and rectangles of every positive area for a one-colour plane. After Mathlib compatibility adjustments and removal of an unused failed proof attempt, the cited external proof also proves the exact type of the file's main theorem; its checked axioms are only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. No status discrepancies were found. Experiments are under /workspace/review/; no repository files were edited.

not_demonstrated.reason: The reported mismatch is a fixed negative answer where the sources pose an unresolved yes-or-no question. The geometric conditions are nonvacuous and the area formula is correct. An honest proof or disproof of the exact declaration would settle the substantive parallelogram problem; no short demonstration follows from this mismatch.

submission.summary: No trivial proof or disproof was produced, and no trivial_proof.lean file remains.
submission.gave_up_reason: The sole reported mathematical mismatch concerns commitment to an unresolved answer, not a defect yielding a trivial theorem or counterexample. Using the imported sorry-backed declaration would not be an honest demonstration.

submission.summary: Replaced the parallelogram variant’s fixed negation with `answer(sorry) ↔ Erdos189For` and updated its docstring to state the source’s question. Its geometry, area formula, research-open category, and AMS tags are unchanged. Also corrected the reported minor Graham citation typo from pages 89–91 to 89–97. The requested compilation succeeds with only `declaration uses sorry` warnings.
